LEILA: NINOY'S SACRIFICE A REMINDER THAT THE FIGHT CONTINUES

House Deputy Minority Leader and ML Partylist Rep. Leila de Lima on Thursday, August 21, marked Ninoy Aquino Day with a statement underscoring the enduring relevance of the late senator's sacrifice in the struggle for justice and accountability.

"Truth unsettles those who fear accountability. And power, when unchecked, will always try to silence it," de Lima said as she recalled how Ninoy Aquino knowingly faced danger by returning to the Philippines in 1983, only to be assassinated upon his arrival at the Manila International Airport.

She described Aquino's final act as "a spark—one that lit a fire in the hearts of a people ready to rise," and said August 21 continues to live on "in every Filipino who refuses to be silent in the face of repression."

De Lima drew parallels between Aquino's time and the present, saying truth-tellers remain persecuted while institutions are "bent to serve a few." Citing her own experience of imprisonment and political persecution, she said she has come to know this kind of courage intimately—"from behind bars, in courtrooms, and in the long hours of waiting for justice to catch up."

"They can delay justice. They can distort history. They can try to convince us that silence is safety. But the memory of August 21 reminds us: there is power in standing up. There is power in telling the truth. And there is power in never giving up," she said.

De Lima concluded her statement by echoing Ninoy's words: "Ninoy believed the Filipino was worth dying for. What his story teaches us today is that the fight continues, and the cause lives on in each of us who refuses to look away. The fire has not gone out."
